violations.msg: Bottom-right board corner (where screw terminal J1 sits) has no mounting hole nearby: H3 is inset 14.3 mm from the right edge (vs the top pair H1/H2's true 4.0 mm corner inset) because J1/J3 own the bottom edges. J1 - the connector that takes repeated wire insertion/removal and screw torque at the bench - sits 9.2 mm from its two nearest holes (H2, H3), neither of which pins the corner itself. Not a fabrication defect (FR4 is stiff at this scale, earned geometry is not being second-guessed), but a real bench-reliability question for a board whose terminal will have wires tugged on it repeatedly across 5 boards' worth of use.

0.582 mm2 zero-anchor GND copper island on B.Cu, isolated by a 0.34 mm gap from the main pour (627.14 mm2, 8 anchors), ~0.9 mm from J3 pin 5 (GND) near the bottom-left corner. Independently reproduced via plane_repair.py --flag-only against the built board (not taken on report). Electrically inert (DC-floating, 0 anchors, far below any EMI-relevant frequency on this board) and DRC/check_pdn correctly pass since nothing electrical is wrong - this is a fab-hygiene item: an unexplained isolated sliver closer to a clearance edge case than any other gap on the board, serving no function. For P9 DFM: purge it (delete, or raise the zone's island-removal area threshold past 0.6 mm2 and re-fill) - zero anchors means zero risk of disconnecting anything real.
